plan.chapterName: OpenStax Organic Chemistry, chapter 5: Stereochemistry at Tetrahedral Centers
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a schematic drawing of a polarimeter, laid out as a single optical path running left to right in perspective. At the far left a lit incandescent bulb sits in a socket inside a yellow glow, labeled "Light source", and short red double-headed arrows pointing in many directions emerge from it beneath the label "Unpolarized light". The beam is drawn as a flat pale yellow ribbon that passes through a circular disc with fine vertical striping, labeled "Polarizer", after which the red arrows all lie in a single vertical plane under the label "Polarized light". The ribbon then runs through a horizontal cylinder with a small filling stub on top, drawn with rounded ends and labeled "Sample tube containing organic molecules"; the red arrows inside progressively tip away from vertical as they move along the tube. Beyond the tube the beam meets a second striped disc labeled "Analyzer" and continues to the right, where a heavy red double-headed arrow lies at a slant. A vertical dashed reference line and a curved arrow mark the angle between the two, labeled with the Greek letter alpha, and a drawn eye at the right edge is labeled "Observer". Tracking one ribbon of light through every component makes the tilt of the arrows the quantity to follow. The arrangement shows how the rotation an optically active sample imposes on the plane of polarization is measured.

elements: Incandescent bulb with glass envelope, filament, and screw base seated in a small round socket/stand at far left
Soft yellow radial glow halo around the bulb
Cluster of short red double-headed arrows radiating in many orientations just right of the bulb (unpolarized light)
Flat pale-yellow translucent ribbon representing the light beam, running left to right along the optical axis through every component
Polarizer: upright circular disc with thin dark vertical stripes and a grey rim, centered on the beam
Vertical red double-headed arrows in the beam between polarizer and sample tube (plane-polarized light)
Sample tube: horizontal glass/grey cylinder with rounded (domed) ends, semi-transparent, containing a faint pale-green liquid
Small cylindrical filling stub on top of the sample tube, near its left-of-center top surface
Sequence of red double-headed arrows inside the tube whose tilt increases progressively from vertical at the entrance to the final rotated angle at the exit
Analyzer: second upright striped circular disc with grey rim, downstream of the tube
Outgoing yellow ribbon continuing right of the analyzer
Heavy slanted red double-headed arrow at the exit representing the rotated plane of polarization
Vertical dashed reference line at the exit marking 0° (original polarization plane)
Curved arrow spanning from the dashed line to the tilted red arrow with Greek letter α label
Stylized eye drawn at far right (observer)
Text labels: 'Unpolarized light', 'Light source', 'Polarizer', 'Polarized light', 'Sample tube containing organic molecules', 'Analyzer', 'Observer', 'α'

interactions.label: Sample optical rotation (°)
interactions.teaches: An optically active sample twists the plane of plane-polarized light; the arrows inside the tube tip progressively and the exit plane angle equals the sample's rotation, with sign giving dextro- vs levorotatory.

interactions.label: Analyzer rotation (°)
interactions.teaches: The observer measures α by rotating the analyzer until light is transmitted maximally; the reading only matches the true rotation when the analyzer's transmission axis lines up with the exit plane.

interactions.label: Send a pulse of light down the path
interactions.teaches: Each component acts in turn: the source emits arrows in all orientations, the polarizer keeps only the vertical plane, and the sample tube gradually rotates that plane before it reaches the analyzer.
The beam is a plane of oscillation in 3D, not a flat line on the page — rotating the scene shows the polarization plane standing perpendicular to the propagation direction.

demo_steps.title: Unpolarized light leaves the source
demo_steps.narration: The bulb emits light whose electric field oscillates in every orientation, shown as red double-headed arrows pointing in many directions.

demo_steps.title: Polarizer selects one plane
demo_steps.narration: After the striped polarizer only the vertical plane survives; the arrows between polarizer and tube are all vertical.

demo_steps.title: An inactive sample changes nothing
demo_steps.narration: With optical rotation set to zero, the arrows stay vertical through the whole tube and α = 0°; the analyzer at 0° passes the beam fully.

demo_steps.title: A chiral sample rotates the plane
demo_steps.narration: Set a positive rotation: the arrows tip further and further as they travel through the tube, leaving at +30° from vertical.

demo_steps.title: The observer finds α
demo_steps.narration: Rotating the analyzer to +30° restores maximum brightness — the angle read off the dashed reference line is α, the rotation imposed by the sample.

demo_steps.title: Opposite enantiomer, opposite sign
demo_steps.narration: A rotation of −30° tips the arrows the other way; the analyzer must now be turned to −30°, showing that α carries a sign.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Optical axis along +X, world units: total path ~16 units from bulb at x=-8 to observer's eye at x=+8. Bulb: sphere r=0.55 at x=-7.4, y=0.5, warm yellow #FFE45C emissive, with grey screw base and a pale disc socket (r=0.7, thickness 0.15) at y=-0.4; glow halo = soft yellow sprite r≈1.8 at 25% opacity. Unpolarized arrow cluster: 8 red (#E8232A) double-headed arrows length 0.5, centered at x=-6.2, randomly oriented in the YZ plane plus a few oblique. Beam ribbon: flat plane 0.9 wide in Z, running x=-6.5 to +6.0, pale yellow #F2D98C at ~60% opacity, lying horizontally (in the XZ plane) so it reads as a flat sheet seen from slightly above. Polarizer disc: circle r=1.0, thickness 0.1, centered x=-4.6, standing upright in the YZ plane (normal along X), grey rim #9A9A9A, face filled with ~24 thin dark vertical (Y-direction) stripes on olive-green #7A8A3C. Polarized arrows: 3 vertical red double-headed arrows length 1.4 at x=-4.0, -3.3, -2.6. Sample tube: cylinder radius 0.85, length 4.4, axis along X, centered at x=-0.6, semi-transparent pale grey-green #CFD9CC at 45% opacity, with hemispherical/domed caps at both ends and a small stub cylinder r=0.18, height 0.4 on top at x=-1.2. Inside the tube place 6 red double-headed arrows length 1.3 at x = -2.6, -1.9, -1.2, -0.5, 0.2, 0.9, each rotated about the X axis by fraction i/5 of the sample rotation angle so the twist accumulates left to right. Analyzer disc: identical to polarizer, r=1.0, centered x=2.6, its stripe pattern rotating about X with analyzerAngle. Exit region: heavy red double-headed arrow length 2.0, thickness 0.08, centered x=4.4, tilted in the YZ plane by the sample rotation angle. Vertical grey dashed line from y=-1.3 to y=+1.3 at x=4.4. Curved α arc radius 1.1 in the YZ plane from the dashed vertical to the red arrow, with italic 'α' label just outside the arc. Observer eye: stylized almond outline with dark pupil at x=7.4, y=0, plus two short horizontal grey sight lines running left from it. Palette: red arrows #E8232A, beam #F2D98C, glow #FFF2A0, disc rims and tube hardware #A8A8A8, tube green tint #BFD2BC, text charcoal #222222. Sign convention: positive sample rotation tilts the arrow clockwise as seen by the observer looking back toward the source (dextrorotatory).
interactionPlan.notes: Render discs as CircleGeometry with a CanvasTexture of vertical stripes; rotate the texture (or the mesh about the X axis) for the analyzer so the striping visibly turns with the slider. Use MeshPhysicalMaterial with transmission/opacity for the sample tube and a DoubleSide transparent MeshBasicMaterial for the beam ribbon so it stays flat and non-shaded. Build each double-headed arrow as a thin cylinder plus two cone tips grouped, then set group.rotation.x to the local polarization angle — makes both sliders and the pulse animation cheap. The glow is an additive-blended sprite, not real lighting. Labels via CSS2DRenderer anchored to their components with small leader lines matching the source (curved leader from 'Sample tube...' up to the tube). The pulse animation drives a normalized t from 0→1 that moves a brighter ribbon segment plus a traveling arrow whose orientation is: random per frame for x<polarizer, vertical between polarizer and tube entrance, lerped to sampleRotation across the tube, fixed after. Analyzer transmission brightness = cos^2(analyzerAngle - sampleRotation) applied to the exit ribbon opacity so misalignment visibly dims the beam. Keep OrbitControls damped with limited polar range so the schematic never flips upside down.

authoredContext:
The angle of rotation can be measured with an instrument called a polarimeter, represented in the figure. A solution of optically active organic molecules is placed in a sample tube, plane-polarized light is passed through the tube, and rotation of the polarization plane occurs. The light then goes through a second polarizer called the analyzer. By rotating the analyzer until the light passes through it, we can find the new plane of polarization and can tell to what extent rotation has occurred.

Schematic representation of a polarimeter. Plane-polarized light passes through a solution of optically active molecules, which rotate the plane of polarization.

Schematic representation of a polarimeter. Unpolarized light from light source passes through polarizer, followed by polarized light, sample tube containing organic molecules, analyzer, and observer.

In addition to determining the extent of rotation, we can also find the direction. From the vantage point of the observer looking directly at the analyzer, some optically active molecules rotate polarized light to the left (counterclockwise) and are said to be levorotatory, whereas others rotate polarized light to the right (clockwise) and are said to be dextrorotatory. By convention, rotation to the left is given a minus sign (−) and rotation to the right is given a plus sign (+). (−)-Morphine, for example, is levorotatory, and (+)-sucrose is dextrorotatory.

discrepancies: Camera/composition: the source lays the optical train out nearly horizontally left-to-right with a mild oblique tilt, while the generated view runs the beam as a steep top-left to bottom-right diagonal, and the whole apparatus occupies only ~30% of the canvas, so the layout reads quite differently at a glance.

The polarizer and analyzer discs are rendered in a dark olive/near-black striped texture, whereas the source shows pale green/teal striped filters with a bright grey bezel — the discs dominate as dark blobs instead of light filters.

The unpolarized 'star' of red arrows at the bulb (a prominent, large multi-direction burst in the source) is almost invisible: the 0.5-unit arrows are dwarfed by the polarizer and are not readable as an all-orientations symbol.

The bulb/light source is much smaller and simpler relative to the rest of the train than in the source, and the yellow glow halo is barely present, losing the strong yellow emission cue of the original.

Labels are all present but rendered at a size that is uncomfortably small against the zoomed-out scene, so key annotations ('Polarizer', 'Analyzer', 'Sample tube containing organic molecules') are hard to read, unlike the large bold captions in the source.
The red exit arrow and α arc region is compressed near the eye; in the source the heavy red exit arrow, dashed vertical reference and α arc form a clear, large angular-measurement inset.
evaluation.notes: All the polarimeter components (bulb, polarizer, sample tube with progressively tipping arrows, analyzer, α arc, observer eye) are modelled in real 3D with excellent, conceptually correct interactions (rotation sliders, Malus-law readout, pulse animation, 6-step narration), but the default camera renders the train as a small steep diagonal with dark discs and tiny labels, so it resembles the source only loosely at a glance.

feedback.rationale: The conceptual decomposition and interactions are correct; the issues are execution-level (default camera framing, component scale, disc/bulb coloring, label sizes), which are generator fixes.

Beam ribbon: flat plane 0.9 wide in Z, running x=-6.5 to +6.0, pale yellow #F2D98C at ~60% opacity, lying horizontally (in the XZ plane) so it reads as a flat sheet seen from slightly above. Polarizer disc: circle r=1.0, thickness 0.1, centered x=-4.6, standing upright in the YZ plane (normal along X), grey rim #9A9A9A, face filled with ~24 thin dark vertical (Y-direction) stripes on olive-green #7A8A3C. Polarized arrows: 3 vertical red double-headed arrows length 1.4 at x=-4.0, -3.3, -2.6. Sample tube: cylinder radius 0.85, length 4.4, axis along X, centered at x=-0.6, semi-transparent pale grey-green #CFD9CC at 45% opacity, with hemispherical/domed caps at both ends and a small stub cylinder r=0.18, height 0.4 on top at x=-1.2. Inside the tube place 6 red double-headed arrows length 1.3 at x = -2.6, -1.9, -1.2, -0.5, 0.2, 0.9, each rotated about the X axis by fraction i/5 of the sample rotation angle so the twist accumulates left to right. Analyzer disc: identical to polarizer, r=1.0, centered x=2.6, its stripe pattern rotating about X with analyzerAngle. Exit region: heavy red double-headed arrow length 2.0, thickness 0.08, centered x=4.4, tilted in the YZ plane by the sample rotation angle. Vertical grey dashed line from y=-1.3 to y=+1.3 at x=4.4. Curved α arc radius 1.1 in the YZ plane from the dashed vertical to the red arrow, with italic 'α' label just outside the arc. Observer eye: stylized almond outline with dark pupil at x=7.4, y=0, plus two short horizontal grey sight lines running left from it. Palette: red arrows #E8232A, beam #F2D98C, glow #FFF2A0, disc rims and tube hardware #A8A8A8, tube green tint #BFD2BC, text charcoal #222222. interactionPlan.notes: Render discs as CircleGeometry with a CanvasTexture of vertical stripes; rotate the texture (or the mesh about the X axis) for the analyzer so the striping visibly turns with the slider. Use MeshPhysicalMaterial with transmission/opacity for the sample tube and a DoubleSide transparent MeshBasicMaterial for the beam ribbon so it stays flat and non-shaded. Build each double-headed arrow as a thin cylinder plus two cone tips grouped, then set group.rotation.x to the local polarization angle — makes both sliders and the pulse animation cheap. The glow is an additive-blended sprite, not real lighting. Labels via CSS2DRenderer anchored to their components with small leader lines matching the source (curved leader from 'Sample tube...' up to the tube). The pulse animation drives a normalized t from 0→1 that moves a brighter ribbon segment plus a traveling arrow whose orientation is: random per frame for x<polarizer, vertical between polarizer and tube entrance, lerped to sampleRotation across the tube, fixed after. Analyzer transmission brightness = cos^2(analyzerAngle - sampleRotation) applied to the exit ribbon opacity so misalignment visibly dims the beam. Keep OrbitControls damped with limited polar range so the schematic never flips upside down.

plan.authoredPrompt: This figure is a schematic drawing of a polarimeter, laid out as a single optical path running left to right in perspective. At the far left a lit incandescent bulb sits in a socket inside a yellow glow, labeled "Light source", and short red double-headed arrows pointing in many directions emerge from it beneath the label "Unpolarized light". The beam is drawn as a flat pale yellow ribbon that passes through a circular disc with fine vertical striping, labeled "Polarizer", after which the red arrows all lie in a single vertical plane under the label "Polarized light". The ribbon then runs through a horizontal cylinder with a small filling stub on top, drawn with rounded ends and labeled "Sample tube containing organic molecules"; the red arrows inside progressively tip away from vertical as they move along the tube. Beyond the tube the beam meets a second striped disc labeled "Analyzer" and continues to the right, where a heavy red double-headed arrow lies at a slant. A vertical dashed reference line and a curved arrow mark the angle between the two, labeled with the Greek letter alpha, and a drawn eye at the right edge is labeled "Observer". Tracking one ribbon of light through every component makes the tilt of the arrows the quantity to follow. The arrangement shows how the rotation an optically active sample imposes on the plane of polarization is measured.

- Slider for changing sample optical activity from zero to a larger positive or negative value; the red arrows inside the tube progressively twist and the final beam angle follows, making rotation of plane-polarized light depend on the organic sample.
- Animation for sending pulses of light from source through polarizer, sample tube, and analyzer; the arrows change from many directions to one plane and then to a tilted plane, clarifying each component's role along the optical path.

discrepancies: The unpolarized-light 'star' of red double-headed arrows at the bulb is rendered so small it reads as a single red smudge; in the source it is a prominent multi-directional arrow burst that carries the 'all orientations' idea.

The α arc between the dashed vertical reference and the exit polarization arrow lies in the YZ plane and is viewed nearly edge-on from the default camera, so it collapses to a dot — the defining angle annotation of the source figure is effectively invisible.

The exit arrow and in-tube arrows show much less apparent tilt than the source because their rotation is about the beam axis seen almost edge-on; the source's dramatic progressive fanning of arrows through the tube (and the fanned arrow cluster past the tube) is weakly conveyed.

The observer eye pictogram and its 'Observer' label sit at the far right against the control panel and are visually clipped/crowded, whereas in the source the observer with its two sight lines and dashed reference is a clear, well-separated element.

Bulb is a plain yellow sphere with no glass envelope/neck silhouette, and the sample tube lacks the curved internal meniscus/lens surfaces visible in the source; simplified but noticeably flatter looking.
Beam ribbon is narrower and ends abruptly rather than extending as the broad golden sheet that reaches the observer's stage in the source.
evaluation.notes: Strong, well-organized reproduction of the polarimeter with correct components, colors, labels and an excellent interaction set (two sliders, pulse animation, 6-step narrated demo, hover notes); main weaknesses are an almost invisible α arc seen edge-on, an undersized unpolarized-arrow star, and weakly visible arrow tilt through the tube.

feedback.rationale: The concept, components, and interaction structure are correct; the issues are rendering details (undersized arrow star, edge-on α arc/camera framing, arrow tilt visibility, crowded observer label) that require implementation fixes rather than a new plan.

Sequence of red double-headed arrows inside the tube whose tilt increases progressively from vertical at the entrance to the final rotated angle at the exit
Analyzer: second upright striped circular disc with grey rim, downstream of the tube
Outgoing yellow ribbon continuing right of the analyzer
Heavy slanted red double-headed arrow at the exit representing the rotated plane of polarization

Curved arrow spanning from the dashed line to the tilted red arrow with Greek letter α label
Stylized eye drawn at far right (observer)

interactions.label: Sample optical rotation (°)
interactions.teaches: An optically active sample twists the plane of plane-polarized light; the arrows inside the tube tip progressively and the exit plane angle equals the sample's rotation, with sign giving dextro- vs levorotatory.

interactions.label: Analyzer rotation (°)
interactions.teaches: The observer measures α by rotating the analyzer until light is transmitted maximally; the reading only matches the true rotation when the analyzer's transmission axis lines up with the exit plane.

interactions.label: Send a pulse of light down the path
interactions.teaches: Each component acts in turn: the source emits arrows in all orientations, the polarizer keeps only the vertical plane, and the sample tube gradually rotates that plane before it reaches the analyzer.
The beam is a plane of oscillation in 3D, not a flat line on the page — rotating the scene shows the polarization plane standing perpendicular to the propagation direction.

demo_steps.title: Unpolarized light leaves the source
demo_steps.narration: The bulb emits light whose electric field oscillates in every orientation, shown as red double-headed arrows pointing in many directions.

demo_steps.title: Polarizer selects one plane
demo_steps.narration: After the striped polarizer only the vertical plane survives; the arrows between polarizer and tube are all vertical.

demo_steps.title: An inactive sample changes nothing
demo_steps.narration: With optical rotation set to zero, the arrows stay vertical through the whole tube and α = 0°; the analyzer at 0° passes the beam fully.

demo_steps.title: A chiral sample rotates the plane
demo_steps.narration: Set a positive rotation: the arrows tip further and further as they travel through the tube, leaving at +30° from vertical.

demo_steps.title: The observer finds α
demo_steps.narration: Rotating the analyzer to +30° restores maximum brightness — the angle read off the dashed reference line is α, the rotation imposed by the sample.

demo_steps.title: Opposite enantiomer, opposite sign
demo_steps.narration: A rotation of −30° tips the arrows the other way; the analyzer must now be turned to −30°, showing that α carries a sign.

discrepancies: The unpolarized-light 'star' of red double-headed arrows next to the bulb collapses into a small red blob in the default view — in the source it is a clearly readable 8-arrow starburst radiating in many directions, which is the whole point of that annotation.

The α angle annotation is weaker than the source: the source shows a dashed vertical reference plus a second solid ray and a clear curved arrow head between them; here only the dashed line and a very thin, nearly invisible arc/head are drawn, so the measured angle is hard to read in figure view.

A large translucent pink 'exit plane' rectangle (and a pink polarization sheet near the analyzer) dominates the right-hand third of the image; nothing like it appears in the source and it partially swamps the exit arrow and observer.

The tan beam ribbon is much fainter and thinner than the prominent continuous yellow-tan light sheet that runs the length of the source figure, weakening the visual thread that ties bulb → polarizer → tube → analyzer → eye.

The bulb is a plain yellow sphere on a grey disc rather than the recognizable incandescent bulb silhouette with screw base and halo, and the observer's eye pictogram sits at the very right edge partly against the control panel.
Arrows inside the sample tube show only a modest progressive tilt and are more numerous/uniform than the source, where the arrows fan out and swing visibly across the tube's length toward the exit.
evaluation.notes: A recognizable, well-composed 3D polarimeter with correct Malus-law physics and a rich, genuinely useful control set (rotation sliders, pulse animation, plane toggle, observer view, 6-step narration); main weaknesses are the illegible unpolarized arrow star, a faint α arc, a fainter beam ribbon than the source, and added pink polarization sheets that clutter the right side.
action_items: Enlarge and re-orient the unpolarized arrow star so the individual double-headed arrows read distinctly (spread them in the YZ plane facing the camera, lengthen to ~1.2 and thin the radius) instead of merging into a red blob.

Strengthen the α annotation: thicken the arc tube and cone head, add the second solid ray from the vertex along the rotated plane (as in the source), and keep the arc oriented so it reads at a glance in the default figure view.

Increase opacity/width of the tan beam ribbon so it forms a continuous light sheet from bulb to observer, and reduce the opacity/size of the pink exit-plane sheets (or default the 'Show polarization plane' checkbox off) so they don't dominate the right side.
Refine the light source: use a bulb-shaped profile (lathe/sphere + neck + screw base) and nudge the observer eye left so it sits clear of the panel edge with its two sight lines.

feedback.rationale: The concept, decomposition, and interaction structure are correct; all action items are concrete rendering fixes (arrow star legibility, α arc emphasis, beam opacity, removing clutter sheets, bulb/eye placement).
